CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  CONTINUED FROM
  APRIL 14, 2026 TO APRIL 20, 2026
  MINUTES
  MONDAY, APRIL 20, 2026
CALL TO ORDER  Joshua Barron, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  5:30 p.m.

INVOCATION  Tina De La Rosa, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Jon F. Hamilton, Director of Human Resources

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Joshua Barron, Vice Mayor Al Rios, Council Member Maria del
  Pilar Avalos, Council Member Gil Hurtado, and Council Member Maria
  Davila; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Rob Houston, City
  Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

PRESENTATION

1
BUDGET ADMIN  The City Council received and filed a presentation on Budget Reduction
  from Community Development, Parks & Recreation, Administration/City
  Clerk and Action by Council.

  Staff’s recommendation, the additions of maintaining programs proposed
  by the Vice Mayor and retaining the pre-sale inspection were approved by
  motion of Mayor Barron and seconded by Vice Mayor Rios.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, no; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  yes.

2
ELECTION ADMIN/
BUDGET ADMIN  The City Council approved items A & B by motion of Council Member
  Davila and seconded by Council Member Hurtado:

  a. Adopting Resolution No. 2026-14-CC submitting ballot measure text
  for the Utility Users Tax Measure to the Voters at the November 3,
  2026 General Municipal Election, request that the Los Angeles County
  Board of Supervisors (“Board of Supervisors”) authorize the Los
  Angeles County Registrar-Recorder / County Clerk (“County
  Elections Official”) to render all services necessary to conduct the
  Election, allow for Ballot Arguments, and an Impartial Analysis; and
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026
2
ELECTION ADMIN/
BUDGET ADMIN
CONT’D
  b. Reviewing the draft Ordinance for voter consideration of the Utility
  Users Tax.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, no; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  yes.

RECESS  Prior to the conclusion of item 2, the City Council recessed at 6:52 p.m.,
  and reconvened at 7:00 p.m., with all Members of Council present.

  IN PERSON PUBLIC COMMENT:

  Thomas Buckley expressed concerns regarding the proposed Utility Users
  Tax (UUT), stating that the increase would financially burden residents
  through increased utility and telecommunications costs. Mr. Buckley also
  disagreed with the characterization of the City’s financial condition as a
  “fiscal emergency,” and commented on the City’s fiscal management and
  prior financial reports regarding projected deficits.

  Nelson Hermocillo commented on consultant services related to Dorothy
  Avenue, expressing concern regarding the cost of the consultant contract
  and requesting that the consultant publicly present the results of its survey
  or study. Mr. Hermosillo also commented on the proposed Utility Users
  Tax (UUT), stating that while additional revenue may be needed, the city
  should further evaluate and reduce expenditures, including conference
  travel, memberships, printing, and mailing costs. Mr. Hermosillo
  encouraged the City Council and department directors to exercise greater
  budget scrutiny and expressed concern regarding the City’s long-term
  financial sustainability.

  Yancy Lopez, a South Gate business owner, spoke in opposition to the
  proposed 7% Utility Users Tax (UUT) and against placing the measure on
  the ballot. Mr. Lopez expressed concern regarding the financial impact the
  tax would have on residents and small businesses through increased utility
  costs and stated that the tax would disproportionately affect lower-income
  households. Mr. Lopez also commented on the City’s budget deficit,
  stating that additional review of internal spending decisions and fiscal
  management should occur prior to implementing a new tax measure.
  Additionally, Mr. Lopez questioned the survey data referenced in support
  of the proposal, noting that the survey represented a small percentage of
  the City’s population.

  Page 2 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026

IN PERSON PUBLIC
COMMENT CONT’D  Jennifer Daly, representing the nonprofit organization Sell for a Better
  Tomorrow, spoke in opposition to the proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT).
  Ms. Daly expressed concerns regarding the City’s budget deficit,
  transparency related to the consultant survey concerning the proposed tax,
  and the City’s code enforcement efforts involving truck yard operations.
  Ms. Daly also commented on public safety concerns, City expenditures,
  and accountability, and urged the city to release additional information and
  improve transparency prior to placing a tax measure before voters.

  Jimmy Ozaeta, a South Gate resident, spoke in opposition to the proposed
  Utility Users Tax (UUT), expressing concerns regarding the City’s fiscal
  management, budget decisions, and use of reserve funds. Mr. Ozaeta
  commented on prior staffing and hiring decisions, the financial challenges
  faced by residents and local businesses, and the potential impact of the
  proposed tax on the community. Mr. Ozaeta further stated that he did not
  believe the UUT represented a long-term financial solution for the City.

  Liz Ruiz, a South Gate resident and property owner, spoke in support of
  placing the proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT) measure on the ballot. Ruiz
  shared personal experiences regarding financial hardship and stated that he
  previously supported Measure P due to the importance of funding City
  services and programs. Ruiz expressed support for maintaining public
  services, parks, public safety, and infrastructure improvements, and
  encouraged the community to support the proposed measure to assist the
  City with ongoing financial challenges and service needs.

  Robert Montalvo, a South Gate resident, spoke in opposition to the
  proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT) and expressed concerns regarding
  transparency, consultant expenditures, and City spending practices. Mr.
  Montalvo commented on the use of Measure P funds, the City’s financial
  management, and the potential impact of the proposed tax on low-income
  residents. Mr. Montalvo also referenced a prior Public Records Act request
  and stated concerns regarding accountability and public trust.

  Brandon Williams, representing MEA and City employees, spoke in
  support of the proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT). Mr. Williams
  commented that neighboring cities also impose utility users' taxes and
  expressed the view that South Gate residents already contribute to similar
  taxes when spending money in surrounding communities. Mr. Williams
  also addressed concerns regarding City spending and fiscal management,
  stating that allegations of overspending or corruption should be supported
  by evidence and encouraging further discussion based on documented
  financial information.

  Page 3 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026
IN PERSON PUBLIC
COMMENT CONT’D  Edgar Pelayo commented on the proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT),
  comparing the proposed measure to Measure P and expressing concerns
  regarding how prior tax revenues were utilized. The speaker questioned
  whether funds generated from previous measures resulted in visible
  improvements to public safety, parks, youth programs, streets, and other
  community services, and expressed concerns regarding transparency,
  accountability, and public trust related to City spending. The speaker also
  stated that discussions regarding the measure should occur publicly so that
  the community could hear responses to questions regarding the proposed
  tax and use of City funds.

  Robin Logan, a South Gate resident, spoke in support of moving forward
  with consideration of the proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT) measure. Ms.
  Logan commented on the City’s financial challenges, public safety
  services, insurance and liability costs, and the importance of maintaining
  City services and staffing levels. Ms. Logan also expressed concern
  regarding delays in addressing the City’s fiscal issues and encouraged the
  community to prioritize funding for essential services and public safety.

  David Berrios expressed support for the proposed Utility Users Tax
  (UUT), stating that the measure would provide a stable funding source for
  essential City services, including public safety, streets, and other
  municipal services. The speaker further commented that the tax would
  distribute costs among users of utility services and emphasized the
  importance of transparency and accountability.

  Joanna Monterosa, Vice President of the Professional Mid-Management
  Association, spoke in support of the proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT).
  Ms. Monterosa commented on the City’s rising insurance costs and
  financial challenges and stated that the UUT would help maintain City
  services and progress achieved in recent years. Ms. Monterosa also
  expressed concern regarding misinformation shared on social media and
  encouraged the City Council to move forward with the proposed measure.

  Richard Ludt, a South Gate resident, spoke regarding the City’s financial
  condition and the proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT). Mr. Lute stated that
  the City’s revenues have remained largely unchanged since 2008 while
  operational costs, including insurance, have increased significantly. Mr.
  Lute expressed support for providing voters the opportunity to consider
  the proposed measure and commented that the City should improve its
  public communication regarding the causes of the current fiscal challenges
  and the need for additional revenue.

  IN PERSON PUBLIC COMMENT CLOSED:

  Page 4 of 13
 REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026

  EMAILED COMMENTS RECEIVED

  The City Clerk reported receipt of written correspondence regarding the
  proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT). Correspondence included opposition to
  the proposed measure, concerns regarding senior exemption provisions,
  questions regarding the use of funds and the City’s long-term financial
  planning, and comments regarding the timing of the proposed tax measure
  and potential appointments to the ad hoc community finance committee.
  The City Clerk further noted that correspondence from Robert Montalvo
  would not be read into the record as Mr. Montalvo was present at the
  meeting and provided public comment.

  BACK TO COUNCIL FOR COMMENTS

  Councilwoman Davila stated that the city is facing a fiscal emergency and
  expressed support for moving forward with placing the proposed Utility
  Users Tax (UUT) measure on the November ballot. Councilwoman Davila
  commented on the City’s rising operational costs, the need to maintain
  City services, and the importance of educating the community regarding
  the proposed measure. Councilwoman Davila further stated that the city
  had been operating with the same revenue structure since 2008 despite
  increased costs and made a motion to place the proposed measure on the
  ballot.

  Councilmember Avalos acknowledged community participation and
  concerns regarding public trust, transparency, accountability, and the
  City’s long-term financial planning. Councilmember Avalos noted that
  while City revenues have increased since 2008, expenditures have
  increased at a greater rate. Councilmember Avalos further discussed
  concerns regarding the potential financial impact on residents, the absence
  of guarantees regarding future financial needs, and the possibility of
  including a sunset provision for the proposed measure. Councilmember
  Avalos also questioned whether additional funding generated from
  Measure P had resulted in dedicated funding for streets and sidewalks and
  discussed the City’s current fiscal limitations. Additionally,
  Councilmember Avalos expressed concern regarding exemption provisions
  within the proposed ordinance, noting that low-income families were not
  included in the exemption language and questioning how senior
  exemptions would be guaranteed and implemented.

  Vice Mayor Rios thanked the public for their participation and discussed
  the City’s ongoing fiscal challenges, noting that many other cities and
  public agencies are experiencing similar financial pressures. Vice Mayor
  Rios stated that operational costs, including pensions and insurance, have
  increased significantly over time while City revenues have not kept pace.

  Page 5 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026

BACK TO COUNCIL
FOR COMMENTS
CONT’D  Vice Mayor Rios further commented that the proposed Utility Users Tax
  (UUT) would provide additional revenue needed to maintain City services
  and programs and emphasized that the proposed measure would ultimately
  be decided by voters. Vice Mayor Rios also addressed concerns raised
  regarding City spending, Measure P revenues, and allegations of financial
  mismanagement, stating that the City has attempted to address fiscal
  challenges while minimizing impacts on residents. Additionally, Vice
  Mayor Rios referenced the formation of a citizens’ ad hoc finance
  committee and expressed support for continued financial planning and
  community outreach regarding the proposed measure.

  Councilmember Hurtado discussed the City’s limited share of property tax
  revenues and ongoing structural budget deficit, noting that rising
  operational costs and stagnant revenues have impacted the City for many
  years. Councilmember Hurtado referenced discussions with the Los
  Angeles County Assessor regarding the City’s financial limitations and
  stated that the City has historically operated with frozen and unfilled
  positions in an effort to live within its financial means. Councilmember
  Hurtado further discussed the adoption of Measure P, stating that it was
  approved to address increasing service demands and rising costs.
  Councilmember Hurtado stated that placing the proposed Utility Users Tax
  (UUT) measure on the ballot would allow voters to determine whether
  additional revenue should be generated to maintain City services and
  programs. Additionally, Councilmember Hurtado addressed concerns
  regarding misinformation related to City expenditures and encouraged
  residents to review publicly available financial documents and participate
  in discussions regarding the City’s finances.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE – NON-AGENDA
ITEMS  Robin Logan expressed concerns regarding pedestrian safety after
  describing a recent incident involving a vehicle failing to stop while the
  resident was lawfully crossing the street at a signalized intersection. The
  resident stated that they do not feel safe walking within the community
  and encouraged additional traffic enforcement, public safety measures,
  and staffing resources, including police and code enforcement personnel.
  The resident also expressed appreciation for the Council’s consideration of
  pedestrian safety improvements and made lighthearted comments
  regarding the length of Council meetings.

  Jimmy Ozaeta, a South Gate resident, spoke regarding concerns related to
  transparency and public trust. He referenced expenditures associated with
  the South Gate Police Department mounted unit and stated concerns
  regarding prior statements about related City costs. Ozaeta also
  commented on a Public Records Act request concerning survey results

  Page 6 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE – NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT’D  related to the proposed Utility Users Tax (UUT), expressing concerns
  regarding the availability of survey documentation and the release of
  taxpayer-funded information. He further stated concerns regarding
  accountability, disclosure of public information, and public confidence in
  City governance.

  Edgar Pelayo commented on the proposed Habitat for Humanity project
  on Long Beach Boulevard and requested additional public information
  regarding the project’s funding sources, including City contributions, use
  of City-owned property, and potential use of Community Development
  Block Grant (CDBG) funds. The speaker also requested information
  regarding anticipated property tax revenue generated by the project and
  expressed interest in a public presentation outlining the project’s financial
  impact, community benefits, transparency, and accountability.

  Jennifer Daly, representing SELA for a Better Tomorrow, commented on
  issues related to transparency and accountability concerning the City’s
  finances. Ms. Daly asked whether the City would consider conducting an
  independent forensic audit in addition to standard annual financial audits
  and questioned whether additional review should occur prior to raising
  taxes on residents.

  Liz Ruiz commented on the potential reduction of City-sponsored events
  and programs due to the City’s financial challenges. Mrs. Ruiz expressed
  appreciation for Parks and Recreation staff and shared positive
  experiences attending City events with her family, including recent Easter
  activities. Ms. Ruiz also encouraged continued community engagement
  and attendance at City events by Councilmembers.

  The City Clerk reported receipt of written correspondence from Osbaldo
  Pichardo regarding allegations that audio from February 24, 2026, City
  Council meeting had been altered. Mr. Pichardo stated that the recording
  originated from the City’s official YouTube broadcast and requested
  transparency and clarification regarding whether an investigation had been
  conducted.

  The City Clerk reported receipt of written correspondence from Mario
  Dominguez regarding virtual meeting platforms. Mr. Dominguez
  expressed concern regarding staff recommendations related to Microsoft
  Teams versus Zoom and advocated for the return of Zoom for public
  meetings, stating that the decision should prioritize public access and
  community input.

  Page 7 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026
COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE – NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT’D  The City Clerk reported receipt of written correspondence from Armando
  Velasquez, on behalf of South Gate Colonies, announcing that the Golden
  Apple Heart of Hero Award ceremony had been rescheduled to May 29
  due to delays related to LAUSD nominations. Mr. Velasquez also provided
  updated event, sponsorship, and ticket information.

  The City Clerk reported receipt of written correspondence from Anthony
  Madrid, a South Gate resident and business owner, providing
  recommendations related to transparency, economic development,
  workforce initiatives, and infrastructure investment intended to support
  balanced growth and community outcomes.

  The City Clerk reported receipt of written correspondence from Robert
  Montalvo regarding the City’s response to a Public Records Act request
  concerning a Teams events contract and matters related to the proposed
  Utility Users Tax (UUT). Mr. Montalvo questioned the lack of supporting
  documentation and requested confirmation that a comprehensive records
  search had been conducted.

  The City Clerk reported receipt of written correspondence from Claudia
  Rivera regarding Councilmember reimbursement and expense practices.
  Ms. Rivera expressed concerns related to fiscal responsibility and
  referenced Councilmember meal, travel, and reimbursement expenditures.
REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Public Works Director Cervantes reported that he had nothing to report.

  Parks and Recreation staff provided updates regarding recent and
  upcoming community programs and events, including the Easter Fest and
  Easter Splash events, Teen Discovery trips, golf night activities, new
  recreation programs at Eastside Park and the new park site, yoga and
  pickleball classes, upcoming art classes, the Miss South Gate pageant,
  Special Olympics activities, the museum art exhibit, the Spring Fun Run,
  the Feet Soccer USA grand opening, JA Opening Day, the Artists Fitness
  Expo, Parks Open House, and the upcoming Mariachi Festival. Staff also
  thanked the City Council for its continued support of Parks and Recreation
  programming.

  Community Development Director Gabriel Perez announced an upcoming
  community engagement meeting regarding the potential repurposing of the
  former courthouse building into a community resilience center. Mr. Perez
  explained that the project could include applying for state grant funding to
  rehabilitate the building for use during emergencies and for community-
  serving programs and activities. The meeting was scheduled for April 30,
  2026, at the Civic Center building.

  Page 8 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Administrative Services Director Frausto reported that he had nothing to
  report.

  Human Resources staff reported that they had nothing to report.

  Police Chief Arana stated that he had no formal report but addressed
  concerns regarding the Police Department mounted unit, noting that the
  intent was for the program to operate as a volunteer and donation-funded
  unit. Chief Arana stated that the matter would be reviewed further
  regarding startup expenses and reimbursement.

  The City Manager addressed concerns related to Public Records Act
  requests and transparency, stating that the City follows established
  procedures for responding to records requests and makes efforts to provide
  responsive documents following legal review. The City Manager further
  stated that the City welcomes public participation and provides
  opportunities for public comment beyond minimum legal requirements.
  Additionally, the City Manager recognized the late Pastor Brady,
  acknowledging his longstanding involvement and contributions to the City
  and community.

  City Treasurer De La Paz requested that staff provide a future presentation
  regarding proposed virtual meeting platforms and related features for
  public meetings. City Treasurer De La Paz also extended birthday wishes
  to the Parks and Recreation Director.

  City Clerk Glaze stated that she had nothing additional to report regarding
  Public Records Act requests and noted that staff were continuing to
  evaluate options related to streaming City meetings and determining the
  best platform for public participation.

  Councilmember Davila reported attending the Easter event, the School
  Safety Collaborative meeting, the State of the County event hosted by
  Supervisor Janice Hahn, the Miss South Gate pageant, and the Street
  Soccer USA grand opening event. Councilmember Davila also announced
  that Hub Cities had been awarded a workforce development contract
  following a multi-year effort and stated that the organization would
  continue working toward strengthening nonprofit funding opportunities
  and financial stability.

  Councilmember Avalos reported attending a Vector Control meeting in
  accordance with AB 1234, during which presentations were provided
  regarding mosquito-borne illnesses, vector control programs, and
  mosquito sterilization efforts intended to reduce disease transmission.

  Page 9 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026
REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Councilmember Hurtado reported attending an event with
  Assemblymember Sade Elhawary and discussions with Los Angeles
  County Assessor Jeff Prang regarding property tax allocations and senior
  protection efforts related to scams and fraud prevention.

  Vice Mayor Rios reported on the recent Hub Cities funding award and
  highlighted the organization’s role in workforce development, job training,
  and internship opportunities within the region. Vice Mayor Rios also
  requested additional information regarding the Habitat for Humanity
  affordable housing project on Long Beach Boulevard, including the
  project’s community benefits and funding structure. Community
  Development Director Perez responded that a formal presentation and
  development agreement would be brought before the City Council and
  noted that the City-owned Housing Authority site would be developed in
  partnership with Habitat for Humanity. Vice Mayor Rios also discussed
  increased parking enforcement efforts by the Police Department following
  community concerns and commented on recent community events
  including the Street Soccer USA grand opening and Earth Day activities.

  Mayor Barron reported attending the California Contract Cities
  Association event recognizing outgoing President Brenda Olmos, the
  Street Soccer USA grand opening, Earth Day activities, and the Miss
  South Gate pageant. Mayor Barron thanked sponsors, volunteers,
  businesses, and community organizations for supporting recent City
  events and youth programs, including scholarship support for participants
  in the Miss South Gate program. Mayor Barron also emphasized the
  importance of community stewardship and environmental awareness.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 were approved by motion of Vice
  Mayor Rios and seconded by Council Member Hurtado except for item 7.
  Council Member Davila seconded item 7. Items 8, 9, 10 and 11 were
  pulled for separate discussion. Council

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Member Hurtado, yes
  (recused from voting on item 7); Council Member Davila, yes (recused
  from voting on item 8); Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron, yes.

   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONTINUED FROM APRIL 14, 2026
  MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2026
3
MUNICIPAL CODE ADMIN  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Find that this action is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to the General Rule Exemption under
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), as there is no possibility that
  the ordinance amendment may have a significant effect on the
  environment, and as a Class 1 Categorical Exemption under CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15301 (Existing Facilities), as the amendment
  involves only a minor change to the administrative hours of operation
  of existing park facilities with no physical alteration to the
  environment. The City Clerk is directed to file a Notice of Exemption
  with the County Clerk within five (5) working days of adoption.

  b. Waived further reading and adopted Ordinance No. 2026-02-CC
  entitled An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of South Gate,
  State of California, amending Section 7.49.150 of Chapter 7.49 of the
  South Gate Municipal Code relating to curfews in municipal parks.

4
MUNICIPAL CODE ADMIN/
ENERGY SAVINGS
PROGRAMS  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent Calendar:

  a. Find that the proposed addition to the South Gate Municipal Code adds
  provisions that are administrative in nature, do not approve any physical
  development, and do not have the potential to result in individually or
  cumulatively significant effects on the environment, and therefore, the
  passage of this ordinance is exempt from California Environmental Quality
  Act ("CEQA") review under the General Rule that CEQA only applies to
  projects with the potential to cause a significant effect on the environment
  and thus no environmental analysis or review is necessary- CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15061(b)(3). The City Clerk is directed to file a Notice of Exemption
  with the County Clerk within five (5) working days of adoption.

  b. Waive further reading and adopt Ordinance No. 2026-03-CC entitled
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of South Gate, California
  amending Title 9 (Buildings) of the South Gate Municipal Code by the
  addition of new Chapter 9.14 establishing a Streamlined Permitting Process
  for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations, consistent with California
  Government Code Section 65850.7 (AB 1236).

STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING  The City Council approved items A, B, C & D during Consent Calendar:

  a. Contract Change Order No. 15 to Contract No. 2024-56-CC with
  Sequel Contractors, Inc., to fund the accelerated construction schedule
  of 145 working days previously approved by the City Council at the
  time of contract award of the Tweedy Mile Complete Streets Project,

  b. Contract Change Order No. 16 to Contract No. 2024-56-CC with

  including bid item overruns and underruns, for the Tweedy Mile

  c. Appropriated $500,000 in Proposition C Funds to fund the cost of
